name: Arizona Biltmore Resort and Spa
insider_take: This Frank Lloyd Wright-influenced desert masterpiece has been the crown jewel of Phoenix since 1929, where Hollywood legends and presidents have retreated to experience authentic Southwestern luxury.
whats_special: The resort's distinctive geometric concrete block design was inspired by Frank Lloyd Wright himself, featuring over 250,000 custom-made blocks. The property sits on 39 pristine acres at the foot of Squaw Peak, offering two championship golf courses and the largest resort pool in Arizona. Its illustrious guest list includes everyone from Irving Berlin to Ronald Reagan.
pro_tip: Book a treatment at the Spa at Arizona Biltmore during sunset hours - the floor-to-ceiling windows offer breathtaking views of the Sonoran Desert as the mountains glow in golden light.
dont_miss: The Wright Bar's legendary cocktail program featuring prickly pear margaritas, and the weekly lawn games on the expansive grounds where you can play croquet or bocce ball against the dramatic desert backdrop. The resort's famous Sunday brunch at Wright's restaurant is a Phoenix institution.
pros: Historic Frank Lloyd Wright-inspired architecture and design heritage
Championship golf courses with stunning desert mountain views
Full-service luxury spa with signature desert-inspired treatments
Multiple pools and extensive resort amenities on 39 acres
cons: Large resort property requires walking between facilities
